title: Prime-power Zolotarev (whole ring): sign(x ↦ a·x on ℤ/pⁿ) = legendreSym p (a mod p)ⁿ = J(a | pⁿ)
description: Closes the prime-power case of the Frobenius/Zolotarev identity, performing the assembly the parent (the units-level prime-power lemma) explicitly left as its follow-up: 'assembling [the units sign] with the action on the non-unit part p·(ℤ/pⁿ⁻¹) ⊂ ℤ/pⁿ to obtain the whole-ring statement sign(ringMulPerm u on ℤ/pⁿ) = J(u | pⁿ), and thence every odd n, is left to the follow-up.' For an odd prime p and a unit a : (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ, the sign of multiplication-by-a on the WHOLE ring ℤ/pⁿ (ZolotarevCRT.ringMulPerm a) equals legendreSym p (a mod p) raised to the n-th power, equivalently the Jacobi symbol J(a | pⁿ). The argument: ringMulPerm a preserves both the units U = {x | IsUnit x} and the non-units N = {x | ¬IsUnit x} = the maximal ideal (p), so its sign factors over the two invariant blocks (Equiv.Perm.sign_subtypeCongr). The units block is the left regular representation Equiv.mulLeft a on (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ, whose sign is legendreSym p (a mod p) — exactly the parent units-level lemma. The non-unit block N = (p) is carried by an additive bijection μ : y ↦ p·(lift y) (nonUnitsEquiv) onto ℤ/pⁿ⁻¹, under which a· becomes multiplication by the reduction ā ∈ (ℤ/pⁿ⁻¹)ˣ; hence its sign is the sign of ringMulPerm ā on the smaller ring — a strictly smaller instance of the same problem. Inducting on n gives legendreSym p (a mod p)ⁿ = J(a | pⁿ).

overview.text: The parent computed the sign of multiplication on the UNITS (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ and flagged the remaining work: glue that to the action on the non-unit part to obtain the whole-ring sign on ℤ/pⁿ. This entry performs exactly that gluing. The key structural fact is that multiplication by a unit a is a permutation of ℤ/pⁿ that maps units to units and non-units to non-units, so by Equiv.Perm.sign_subtypeCongr its sign is the product of the signs of its restrictions to the two blocks. The units block is the parent's left-regular-representation computation; the non-unit block — the maximal ideal (p), of size pⁿ⁻¹ — is additively isomorphic to ℤ/pⁿ⁻¹ via y ↦ p·(lift y), an isomorphism under which the a-action becomes the (ā)-action of the reduced unit, giving an honest recursion on the exponent. The compatibility μ(ā·y) = a·μ(y) — the one genuinely new computation — rests on the elementary bridge p·u = p·v ⟺ u ≡ v (mod pⁿ⁻¹) in ℤ/pⁿ.
overview.historicalContext: Zolotarev (1872) identified the Legendre symbol (a/p) with the sign of x ↦ ax on (ℤ/p)ˣ; Frobenius (1914) generalized this to composite moduli and the Jacobi symbol. The gallery lineage built it up in layers: the great-grandparent (oq-01-oq-03) gave the CRT decomposition of the multiplication-permutation sign on the whole ring ℤ/n; the grandparent (oq-01-oq-03-oq-01) the prime base case on ℤ/p; the squarefree parent (oq-01-oq-03-oq-01-oq-01) the factorization induction over distinct primes (reaching J for all squarefree odd n) and flagged prime powers pᵉ as the obstruction; the units-level parent (oq-01-oq-03-oq-01-oq-01-oq-01) supplied the sign on (ℤ/pᵉ)ˣ and flagged the whole-ring assembly. This entry closes that prime-power case.
overview.problemStatement: Open Question (the listed follow-up of elementary-quadratic-reciprocity-oq-01-oq-03-oq-01-oq-01-oq-01): assemble the units-level prime-power sign with the action on the non-unit part p·(ℤ/pⁿ) ≅ ℤ/pⁿ⁻¹ to obtain the whole-ring statement sign(ringMulPerm a on ℤ/pⁿ) = J(a | pⁿ). This entry proves sign(ringMulPerm a on ℤ/pⁿ) = legendreSym p (a mod p)ⁿ = J(a | pⁿ) for every odd prime p and unit a.
overview.proofStrategy: Part I (bridge): in ℤ/pⁿ⁺¹, p·z = 0 ⟺ z reduces to 0 in ℤ/pⁿ (both say pⁿ ∣ z.val), proved by ZMod.natCast_eq_zero_iff after cancelling one factor of p; this yields p·u = p·v ⟺ castHom u = castHom v (mul_p_of_castHom_eq / castHom_eq_of_mul_p_eq). Part II (non-unit block): p·z is never a unit (not_isUnit_mul_p, via ZMod.isUnit_iff_coprime), and y ↦ p·(lift y) is a bijection ℤ/pⁿ → {non-units of ℤ/pⁿ⁺¹} — injective by the bridge, surjective by cardinality (pⁿ⁺¹ − φ(pⁿ⁺¹) = pⁿ via Nat.totient_prime_pow_succ). Part III (recursion): ringMulPerm a preserves IsUnit (a is a unit, IsUnit.mul_iff), so Equiv.Perm.sign_subtypeCongr factors sign(ringMulPerm a) = sign(units block)·sign(non-unit block); the units block equals sign(Equiv.mulLeft a) = legendreSym p (a mod p) by the parent lemma (transported via the units↔IsUnit-subtype equiv), the non-unit block equals sign(ringMulPerm ā) on ℤ/pⁿ⁻¹ (transported via the μ-bijection, whose intertwining μ(ā·y)=a·μ(y) is the bridge). Part IV: induct on n to get legendreSym p (a mod p)ⁿ, and J(A | pⁿ) = (legendreSym p A)ⁿ (jacobiSym.mul_right) converts it to the Jacobi symbol.
keyInsights: Multiplication by a unit a permutes ℤ/pⁿ while preserving the units / non-units partition, so its sign is the product of the two block signs (Equiv.Perm.sign_subtypeCongr) — the whole-ring problem splits cleanly into the parent's units computation and a smaller copy of itself.

The non-units of ℤ/pⁿ form the maximal ideal (p), of size pⁿ⁻¹, and y ↦ p·(lift y) is an additive bijection ℤ/pⁿ⁻¹ ≅ (p) under which multiplication-by-a becomes multiplication-by-(a mod pⁿ⁻¹) — turning the non-unit block into a strictly smaller instance and giving a genuine recursion on the exponent.

Everything reduces to one elementary bridge in ℤ/pⁿ⁺¹: p·u = p·v ⟺ u ≡ v (mod pⁿ). It supplies both the injectivity of the non-unit isomorphism and the intertwining μ(ā·y) = a·μ(y) that the recursion needs.
The non-unit block's cardinality is exactly pⁿ⁻¹ = pⁿ − φ(pⁿ) = pⁿ − pⁿ⁻¹(p−1), so the p-multiplication map is a bijection by injectivity-plus-counting, no explicit inverse required.

Iterating the one-step recursion n times collapses the whole-ring prime-power sign to legendreSym p (a mod p)ⁿ, and jacobiSym.mul_right identifies this with J(a | pⁿ), closing the prime-power case the squarefree induction could not reach.
prerequisites: The units-level prime-power lemma (ZolotarevPrimePower.sign_mulLeft_eq_legendre) and the whole-ring multiplication permutation ZolotarevCRT.ringMulPerm
Sign of a permutation over an invariant predicate / its complement (Equiv.Perm.sign_subtypeCongr, Equiv.Perm.subtypePerm) and transport of sign across an equiv (Equiv.Perm.sign_eq_sign_of_equiv)
ZMod reduction homomorphism ZMod.castHom / ZMod.unitsMap and ZMod.natCast_eq_zero_iff, ZMod.isUnit_iff_coprime
Cardinality of the unit group (ZMod.card_units_eq_totient, Nat.totient_prime_pow_succ) and Fintype.bijective_iff_injective_and_card
Multiplicativity of the Jacobi symbol over prime powers (jacobiSym.mul_right, legendreSym.to_jacobiSym)

sections.title: The p-multiplication bridge on ℤ/pⁿ⁺¹
sections.content: mul_p_eq_zero_iff: p·z = 0 in ℤ/pⁿ⁺¹ iff z reduces to 0 in ℤ/pⁿ (both express pⁿ ∣ z.val), via ZMod.natCast_eq_zero_iff and cancelling one factor of p (Nat.mul_dvd_mul_iff_left). mul_p_of_castHom_eq and castHom_eq_of_mul_p_eq promote this to p·u = p·v ⟺ castHom u = castHom v — the single fact behind both the non-unit isomorphism and its intertwining.

sections.title: The non-unit block is ℤ/pⁿ⁻¹
sections.content: not_isUnit_mul_p: p·z is never a unit (ZMod.isUnit_iff_coprime). nonUnitsFun / nonUnitsFun_bijective / nonUnitsEquiv: y ↦ p·(lift y) is a bijection ℤ/pⁿ ≃ {non-units of ℤ/pⁿ⁺¹}, injective by the bridge and surjective by counting (pⁿ⁺¹ − φ(pⁿ⁺¹) = pⁿ).

sections.title: The prime-power recursion for the whole-ring sign
sections.content: sign_ringMulPerm_succ: for a unit a : (ℤ/pⁿ⁺¹)ˣ, sign(ringMulPerm a) = legendreSym p (a mod p) · sign(ringMulPerm ā on ℤ/pⁿ). Proof: sign_subtypeCongr factors the sign over the units / non-units partition; the units block is sign(Equiv.mulLeft a) = legendreSym p (a mod p) (parent lemma, transported via units↔IsUnit-subtype equiv); the non-unit block is sign(ringMulPerm ā) (transported via the μ-bijection, intertwining from the bridge).

sections.title: The prime-power Zolotarev–Frobenius identity
sections.content: sign_ringMulPerm_eq_legendre_pow: iterating the recursion, sign(ringMulPerm a on ℤ/pⁿ) = legendreSym p (a mod p)ⁿ. jacobiSym_prime_pow + sign_ringMulPerm_eq_jacobiSym: J(A | pⁿ) = (legendreSym p A)ⁿ (jacobiSym.mul_right), so the sign equals the Jacobi symbol J(a | pⁿ) — closing the prime-power case.

conclusion.summary: Proves, with 0 sorries and 0 axioms, the whole-ring prime-power Frobenius/Zolotarev identity: for an odd prime p and a unit a : (ℤ/pⁿ)ˣ, the sign of multiplication-by-a on the whole ring ℤ/pⁿ equals legendreSym p (a mod p)ⁿ = J(a | pⁿ). It performs the assembly the units-level parent flagged: factor the sign over the invariant units / non-units partition, identify the units block with the parent's left-regular-representation sign and the non-unit block (the maximal ideal (p) ≅ ℤ/pⁿ⁻¹) with a strictly smaller instance of the same problem, and recurse on the exponent. The one new computation — that the additive isomorphism p·(lift y) intertwines the a-action with the reduced action — reduces to the elementary bridge p·u = p·v ⟺ u ≡ v (mod pⁿ⁻¹).
conclusion.implications: Closes the prime-power obstruction the squarefree induction could not handle. Combined with the great-grandparent's CRT multiplicativity (sign_ringMulPerm_mul_of_odd), it yields sign(ringMulPerm a on ℤ/n) = J(a | n) for EVERY odd n — completing the Frobenius generalization of Zolotarev's lemma — from which quadratic reciprocity itself follows (Zolotarev's original application). The reusable pieces are the p-multiplication bridge in ℤ/pⁿ⁺¹ and the additive isomorphism of the maximal ideal with the smaller ring.
openQuestions: Combine this per-prime-power identity with the great-grandparent's CRT multiplicativity (sign_ringMulPerm_mul_of_odd) and the multiplicativity of the Jacobi symbol to obtain sign(ringMulPerm a on ℤ/n) = J(a | n) for EVERY odd n — a now purely organizational induction over the prime factorization.
Specialize the resulting general-odd Frobenius identity to recover the quadratic reciprocity law itself (Zolotarev's original derivation, via the sign of a suitable shuffle permutation).
Extract the additive isomorphism (p) ≅ ℤ/pⁿ⁻¹ and the p-multiplication bridge as standalone ZMod lemmas of independent interest (filtration of ℤ/pⁿ by the powers of its maximal ideal).
